title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.33745v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models predict what happens under an action, but choosing between actions requires comparing their outcomes in the same physical situation. Factual transitions alone determine action-wise marginal futures and average effects, but not individual effects or the probability that switching actions causes harm. We introduce WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and transition noise inferred from factual history. Each candidate action induces a sparse object-factor causal graph describing the physical pathways it activates. Rolling out these graphs under the shared situation anchors predictions to observed outcomes and confines action contrasts to the objects each action reaches. translated_title: WhatIf：基于动作锚定因果图的机器人操作反事实世界模型
translated_abstract: 世界模型可以预测某个动作下的结果，但在动作之间做出选择需要比较它们在相同物理情境下的结果。仅凭事实性转移只能确定各动作的边缘未来和平均效应，却无法确定个体效应或切换动作造成损害的概率。我们提出了WhatIf，一个面向机器人操作的反事实世界模型，它通过从事实历史中推断出的共享潜在物理和转移噪声来耦合候选未来。每个候选动作都会诱导出一个稀疏的对象因子因果图，用以描述该动作激活的物理路径。在共享情境下滚动展开这些因果图，可以将预测锚定到观测结果上，并将动作对比限制在每个动作所能触及的对象范围内。共享的类型条件函数支持对象数量可变的情形，而往返损失则无需反事实标签即可强制实现动作不变的溯因推理。我们展示了替换…
tldr: 该论文提出WhatIf，一种通过共享潜在物理与动作锚定的稀疏对象因子因果图来耦合候选未来的反事实世界模型，能够在无需反事实标签的情况下比较不同动作在相同物理情境中的个体效应。
en_tdlr: WhatIf is a counterfactual world model for robotic manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and sparse action-grounded object-factor causal graphs, enabling comparison of individual action effects in identical physical situations without requiring counterfactual labels.
